title: get_list checks user_id but field is actually persona_id
description: api.rs:1286. In get_list, the list ownership check is l.user_id == auth.account_id. The auth.account_id is the persona ID (from the token -> persona mapping). If lists_db stores the persona_id in user_id column, this works correctly. But if user_id is the tenant user ID (DEFAULT_USER_ID = 1000000000001), the comparison will always fail since auth.account_id is a persona ID. The same pattern appears in get_list_accounts (line 1374), add_list_accounts (line 1412), remove_list_accounts (line 1444), delete_list (line 1350), update_list (line 1317), and filter operations. All depend on whether fieldwork stores persona_id or tenant user_id in the user_id column.
close_reason: create_list and get_lists both use auth.account_id consistently. The ownership check is correct as long as fieldwork stores the same value in user_id that it filters by. The naming is confusing but not a bug.
